notes.text: Santa suits on from the front door. Passports all day: tax-free at LUCUA and ID checks at the bars and Round1. Only overnight bags once the suitcases are with TA-Q-BIN.
Cold all day, dark by early evening, and freezing on the Umeda Sky roof and in Dotonbori before dawn. Wear layers under the suit, plus gloves.
Today's trains are Osaka Metro and Kintetsu, not JR, so tap IC cards. The big spend is the wagyu dinner.

stops.summary: Suitcases off to Tokyo by TA-Q-BIN, konbini breakfast, and out the door in full Santa.
stops.story: Today you travel light: the big bags go to Garfield House in Shinjuku for Saturday evening, so all you carry is an overnight bag and a Santa hat. Eight Santas on the morning Metro is a fair preview of how the day will go.
how: Fill in the TA-Q-BIN slips to Garfield House for Sat 26 evening delivery and hand the cases over.
Konbini breakfast on the way to the station.
Chuo line 09:10 from Kujō to Nagata, Kintetsu through Ikoma, then the express into Kintetsu-Nara at 10:04.
tips: Pull out passports, chargers and tomorrow's clothes before the cases go.
The route is Metro plus Kintetsu (¥910) on your IC card, not the JR pass.
wishes: Osaka base, but during the day we will commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed

stops.summary: Eight Santas under the Great Buddha, then crawl through the pillar behind it.
stops.story: The Great Buddha Hall is a colossal wooden hall with a giant bronze Buddha that makes everyone go quiet, even in Santa suits. Behind it is a pillar with a hole at the base: squeeze through and you're supposedly blessed, or at least filmed by seven friends.
how: Pay at the hall (¥800).
Buddha first, then round the back to the pillar.
Take the eight-Santa photo outside on the approach.
tips: No group photos or tripods inside, so save the posing for outside.
Open 07:30–17:30. The cold morning is the time to beat the tour buses.
wishes: Christmas Day in Santa suits, the whole group, ending in a Round1 all-nighter in Osaka

stops.summary: Buy shika senbei and get mugged by bowing deer: Santas being chased is the photo of the trip.
stops.story: Nara's deer bow politely for crackers, then headbutt you the second you run out, and they have no respect for a Santa suit. The park is brown and bare in December, which makes eight red suits look even better.
how: Buy shika senbei (¥200) from a vendor deeper in the park.
Bow, wait for the bow back, hand one over.
When you run out, show empty hands and walk off.
tips: Keep the crackers hidden until you're ready, or the deer go for your bags and pom-poms.
Nakatanidō is a 20 min walk west along Noborioji.
wishes: Christmas Day in Santa suits, the whole group, ending in a Round1 all-nighter in Osaka

stops.summary: Watch mochi pounded at an insane speed, then eat it warm in the street.
stops.story: Nakatanidō is famous for its high-speed mochi pounding: mallets and bare hands trading places so fast every beat looks like an accident. The yomogi mochi comes out soft and warm, and it's perfect in cold air. It's a snack, not lunch.
how: See if a pounding round is on and get a spot out front.
One yomogi mochi each (¥200).
Kintetsu express 13:11 from Kintetsu-Nara to Osaka-Namba (13:50), then Midosuji line 13:56 to Umeda (14:04).
tips: Irregular closing days are posted on Instagram, so check that morning.
Eat it hot. Mochi stiffens fast in the cold.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Okonomiyaki and yakisoba on a hot griddle in the retro alley under Umeda Sky.
stops.story: Kiji is a tiny griddle counter in Takimi-kōji, the old-Osaka street rebuilt in the basement of the Umeda Sky Building, and it's highly rated on Tabelog. Expect a queue and to sit in two groups; it's worth it for okonomiyaki cooked right in front of you.
how: Go to B1 of the Umeda Sky Building, into Takimi-kōji.
Join the queue (no reservations) and split into two groups as seats free up.
Order okonomiyaki and yakisoba to share, and check the posted prices.
tips: It has about 20 seats and peak waits of 30–60 min, so a late lunch helps.
Closed Thursdays, but Friday is fine.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Nintendo OSAKA on 13F and a fast LUCUA 1100 sweep, passports in hand for tax-free.
stops.story: LUCUA is the young-fashion mall built into JR Osaka Station, full of mid-price Japanese labels and select shops, and Nintendo's official Osaka store is up on 13F of LUCUA South. It's a Christmas Day afternoon, so go in with a target, not a vibe.
how: Nintendo OSAKA first, on 13F.
Split by floor through LUCUA 1100 and regroup at the exit.
Show passports at the till for tax-free and keep every receipt.
tips: Nintendo can switch to timed-entry tickets on busy days, so check the official store page the day before.
Tax-free paperwork gets finished at the Haneda customs kiosk, so don't lose the receipts.
stops.booking: Nintendo OSAKA may use timed-entry tickets on busy days
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: An open-air ring 173 m up, from sunset into the lit skyline, on the last day of the Christmas event.
stops.story: The Kuchu Teien Floating Garden is an open-air ring bridging two towers, and at sunset (about 16:50) all of Osaka switches on below you. It's also the final day of THE STARLIGHT TOWN, the building's Christmas event, with decorations up top and a market at ground level.
how: Buy tickets at the observatory (about ¥2,000; check the price on the site).
Get onto the open roof before sunset and stay until it's fully dark.
Leave at 17:35 for the 17:56 Midosuji train to Yodoyabashi.
tips: The Osaka Amazing Pass only gets you in free before 15:00, so at this hour you pay.
It's windy and bitter up top, so keep the gloves on.
Expect an evening queue for the lift on 24–25 Dec.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Free projection mapping on the Central Public Hall, and it's the final night.
stops.story: Nakanoshima's red-brick Central Public Hall becomes a screen for the Hikari Renaissance projection mapping, and tonight is the last night of the run. Watching an old landmark melt into light in a crowd of locals, dressed as Santa, is a strong start to Christmas night.
how: Walk from Yodoyabashi to the Central Public Hall.
Each show is about 10 min and repeats every 12 min, so if you just missed one, wait.
Back to Yodoyabashi for the 18:59 Midosuji train to Shinsaibashi (19:02).
tips: The run ends 25 Dec, so tomorrow it's gone.
The Hikari Marche stalls run alongside on the same final night.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Walk the lit ginkgo avenue south from Shinsaibashi: eight Santas on parade, straight to dinner.
stops.story: The ginkgos on Midosuji are bare in late December, but they're wrapped in lights the whole way from Umeda to Namba, Osaka's main Christmas-week backdrop. You only do the Shinsaibashi stretch, a short parade that ends at dinner.
how: Come up at Shinsaibashi and walk south on Midosuji.
Stop mid-avenue for the group shot.
Dinner is a 2 min walk away.
tips: The lights stay on until 01:00, so the walk to Round1 later gets them too.
wishes: Christmas Day in Santa suits, the whole group, ending in a Round1 all-nighter in Osaka

stops.summary: A5 Matsusaka beef Christmas dinner in a private room: the big-ticket meal of the trip.
stops.story: The Premium course is A5 Matsusaka start to finish: beef sushi, 4 grilled cuts, shabu-shabu sukiyaki, garlic rice and dessert. You grill it yourselves at the table, which with eight Santas and drinks gets loud fast.
how: Booked via Japan Food Guide: Premium course, private room for 8.
Be on time, because 30 min late can count as a no-show.
A5 needs a quick sear, not a long grill, so don't walk away from it.
tips: Free cancellation until the day before, so lock the headcount by then.
Don't fill up on garlic rice before the sukiyaki.
stops.booking: Japan Food Guide (English, replies within 48 h); free cancel until the day before
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Free Famicom, N64 and PlayStation with themed cocktails: Santa versus Santa at Mario Kart.
stops.story: A tiny bar with walls of old consoles that you play free while you drink. Eight Santas will fill it, so rotate the controllers and trash-talk from the bar.
how: Walk 9 min west across Midosuji into Amerikamura.
One themed cocktail each, plus the usual small table charge.
Play in rotating pairs so everyone gets a go.
tips: Drinks run about ¥700–1,000.
Walk-in only and tight, so arrive together, not in waves.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: Konbini toast in Triangle Park, then the tiny bars in the walk-ups around it.
stops.story: Amerikamura is Osaka's youth district and Triangle Park is its open-air living room, and on Christmas night it's packed. Toast with konbini cans, then climb into the small reggae and hip-hop bars in the buildings around it.
how: Konbini run, then meet in Triangle Park (a 3 min walk from Space Station).
Toast, then pick a walk-up bar.
Head for Round1 by 00:30. It's a 13 min walk east.
tips: No clubs (group rule): skip Circus and ignore the club touts.
Bars run ¥500–800 a drink.

stops.summary: The Christmas all-nighter: karaoke or Spo-Cha until the first train, still in the suits.
stops.story: Round1 Sennichimae is a whole building of arcade, karaoke, darts, bowling and Spo-Cha, open all night steps from Dotonbori. This is the wish the whole day was built around: eight Santas screaming into karaoke mics at an hour none of you will admit to.
how: Have passports ready for the night ID check.
The arcade corner closes around 00:50, right when you arrive, so go straight to karaoke or Spo-Cha.
Take the midnight-to-morning karaoke pack (up to 6 h after midnight), split into 2 rooms if needed.
tips: Join the free Round1 app membership for ¥200–350 off Spo-Cha packs.
Friday night means weekend rates, so check the store's fee page.
Under-18s are barred 22:00–05:00, so staff card everyone.
stops.cost: Karaoke from ¥440 pp minimum order + ¥390 drink bar
stops.booking: Optional, via the reservation link on the store page
stops.hours: Open around the clock; arcade corner closes earlier
wishes: Christmas Day in Santa suits, the whole group, ending in a Round1 all-nighter in Osaka

stops.summary: Dragon-sign ramen with free kimchi in the pre-dawn dark: the last scene of Christmas.
stops.story: Kinryu isn't Osaka's best ramen and nobody cares at this hour: it never closes, the dragon sign is lit, and the kimchi and rice are free. Eight Santas slurping on open-air stools while Dotonbori goes quiet is how Christmas ends.
how: Buy tickets at the machine.
Help yourselves to kimchi and rice.
First Hanshin Namba line train 05:42 from Osaka-Namba to Kujō (05:49).
tips: It's still pitch dark and the coldest hour, so eat fast.
Checkout at Kujō House is 10:00, so set alarms before you crash.
